political_impact.text: The order reserved the islets for the Department of Agriculture without naming the Bureau of Biological Survey, the arm of the Department that ran the bird reservations.

Like the bird orders before it, the reservation drew no recorded public reaction; it was one more small addition to the record of executive action that Roosevelt's opponents in Congress and the West resented as government by proclamation.

legacy.text: Taft enlarged the reservation up into the Halifax River in 1909 and added the ban on hunting, trapping, capturing or disturbing birds that Roosevelt's order lacked.
The Biological Survey discontinued the refuge in 1928, saying it had become of little value to birds because of the growth of New Smyrna and a question of jurisdiction.
legacy.source: Report of the Chief of the Bureau of Biological Survey, FY 1928, p. 27

legacy.text: A historical marker at the Ponce de Leon Inlet Lighthouse dates the reservation 1909–1918 and credits Taft, matching neither the 1908 creation nor the 1928 revocation.
Mosquito Inlet counts among the fifty-one bird reservations Roosevelt created by executive order, the body of work that became the National Wildlife Refuge System.

today.name: Mosquito Inlet Reservation
today.note: Revoked in 1928. The inlet, renamed Ponce de Leon Inlet in 1927, lies about ten miles south of Daytona Beach.
today.source: Executive Order 4832; Laws of Florida 1927, ch. 13325

later_actions.text: Taft's Executive Order 1057 enlarged the Mosquito Inlet Reservation and added a ban on hunting, trapping, capturing or disturbing the birds.
The Florida Legislature renamed Mosquito Inlet as Ponce de Leon Inlet.
later_actions.source: Laws of Florida 1927, ch. 13325, vol. III, p. 3783

later_actions.text: Executive Order 4832, under Coolidge, revoked both the 1908 order and Taft's 1909 enlargement.

uncertain: The exact wording of Executive Order 4832 has not been checked against the signed original.
What happened to the birds on the reservation between 1908 and 1928 is not known; a 1909 Bird-Lore warden's report mentioning a Captain Pacetti is an unconfirmed lead.

later_actions.text: Woodrow Wilson's Executive Order 2526 repealed the extension of Panama's Chinese exclusion law to the Canal Zone and substituted a Zone-specific exclusion regime.

political_impact.text: None of these orders drew recorded public reaction; the land-district and Canal Zone orders were pure administration.

legacy.text: The Canal Zone legal framework these orders helped build governed the Zone until the Torrijos–Carter treaties handed the canal to Panama at noon on December 31, 1999.
Under Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1946, the General Land Office whose districts these orders merged joined the Grazing Service to form the Bureau of Land Management.
